i0: *Was* and *were* are the past forms of *be* (*am / is / are*): *I **was** at home yesterday. They **were** late.*
i1: They are some of the most common words in English. This page starts with the basic forms and goes on to the mistakes learners often make with *did*, and to *were* in *If I were you*.
ww-form.t: I was, you were: the forms
ww-form.s: I / he / she / it **was**; you / we / they **were**.
ww-form.b1: Use *was / were* with past time words: *yesterday, last night, last week, two days ago, in 2015, when I was a child*.
ww-form.b2: There are only two forms. **Was** goes with *I, he, she, it* and singular nouns (*my brother was*). **Were** goes with *you, we, they* and plural nouns (*my parents were*). *You* is always **were**, even for one person.
ww-form.n3: you → were, even for one person
ww-negative-questions.s: Negative: **wasn't / weren't**. Questions: **Was** he…? **Were** you…? No *did*.
ww-negative-questions.b0.h: | I / he / she / it | you / we / they
ww-negative-questions.b1: For questions, put *was / were* **before** the subject: *She was tired.* → ***Was** she tired?* With a question word: ***Where were** you? **Why was** he angry? **How was** your weekend?*
ww-negative-questions.b2: Don't use *did* with *was / were*. Not *Did you were at home?* but ***Were** you at home?*
ww-born.t: Was born, was / were + adjective, it was
ww-born.s: *I **was born** in 1995.* (not *I born*). Use *was / were* to describe the past: *It was cold. They were nervous.*
ww-born.b0: To say when or where someone started life, use ***was / were born***: *I **was born** in Tehran. My twins **were born** in May.* Not *I born* or *I am born*.
ww-born.b1: Use *was / were* + adjective or noun to describe things in the past: *The food **was** delicious. The people **were** friendly. My first car **was** a Fiat.*
ww-born.b2: Use ***it was*** for the weather, time and opinions: ***It was** sunny. **It was** 10 o'clock. **It was** a great day.*
ww-born.b3: For something that exists in the past, use ***there was / there were***: ***There was** a problem. **There were** a lot of people.* See [There Is and There Are](/blog/grammar/there-is-there-are/).
ww-vs-did.s: *Was / were* + adjective, noun, place or *-ing*. *Did* + base verb. Don't mix them.
ww-vs-did.b1: Use *was / were* when the main word is an adjective (*tired*), a noun (*a doctor*) or a place (*at home*). Use *did / didn't* with a **verb** (*go, like, see*).
ww-vs-did.b2: Positive sentences with other verbs don't need *was / were*: *I **went** home.* Not *I was go home*. (*Was* + *-ing* is the past continuous: *I **was going** home.* See [Past Continuous](/blog/grammar/past-continuous/).)
ww-if-i-were.t: Were after if and wish: If I were you…
ww-if-i-were.s: In unreal sentences we often use **were** for all persons: *If I **were** you… I wish it **were** Friday.*
ww-if-i-were.b0: In sentences about **unreal** or imaginary situations, we can use ***were*** with *I, he, she, it*: *If I **were** rich, I'd travel the world. I wish she **were** here.*
ww-if-i-were.b1: In everyday speech, *was* is also common here: *If I **was** rich…* Both are correct. ***Were*** is more formal and is the usual choice in writing.
ww-if-i-were.b2: In the fixed phrase for advice, always use ***were***: ***If I were you**, I'd take the job.* (*If I was you* is very informal.)
ww-if-i-were.b3: This *were* is not about the past. It is about now or an imagined situation. See [Second Conditional](/blog/grammar/second-conditional/) and [Wish and If Only](/blog/grammar/wish-if-only/).
